ai.description: *Amolops medogensis* is a 4–5 cm frog with a green-spotted brown dorsum and white belly. It features a distinct white upper lip stripe and granular skin on the flanks. It belongs to family Ranidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops medogensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored supralabial stripe that extends clearly to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: *Amolops medogensis* inhabits high-altitude, fast-flowing mountain streams within subtropical evergreen forests, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Medog Torrent Frog is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for small invertebrates along the rocky, fast-flowing streams of its high-altitude habitat after dark.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops medogensis* is oviparous, laying eggs in aquatic environments. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, though specific clutch sizes remain undocumented.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops medogensis* is found in the Eastern Himalayas of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting high-altitude mountain streams between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Medog Torrent Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "peep" notes while perched on rocks near the fast-flowing streams of its high-altitude forest habitat.
